name: Cinnarizine
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Cinnarizine is extensively metabolized by the liver (CYP2D6); metabolites are excreted about one-third in urine and two-thirds in feces. The Irish label has no kidney studies and advises using it with care in kidney insufficiency, without a dose change. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: The SmPC does not grade kidney impairment; bands shown on creatinine clearance (CrCl).

bands.recommendation: Motion sickness: 30 mg 2 hours before travel, then 15 mg every 8 hours during the journey (SmPC).
No specific studies in kidney impairment; the SmPC says to use with care. Use with caution and specialist judgment.

monitoring: Sedation (worse with alcohol and central nervous system depressants); extrapyramidal symptoms and parkinsonism, especially in older adults on long-term use (SmPC 4.4, 4.8).

pediatric.approved_ages: Motion sickness: 5 to 12 years at half the adult dose (SmPC).
pediatric.usual_dose: 5 to 12 years: half the adult dose.
